diagnosis.root_cause: The nested PrimitiveBytes class keeps static mutable state (`iterations` and `values`) that is never reset between outer test invocations. Each invocation of `primitiveBytes` runs the `@Property` 100 times and increments the same static counter, so on the third run `iterations` is 300 instead of `defaultPropertyTrialCount()`=100, failing the assertion at line 119.

evidence.why: This assertion compares the expected trial count (100) to the accumulated static counter; after repeated runs in the same JVM it becomes 300, producing expected:<100> but was:<300>.
`iterations` and `values` are static fields on the nested class and are mutated by the property method without any reset between test runs, so state persists across invocations in the same JVM.

diagnosis.root_cause: BoxOfFoo.iterations is a static field that is incremented by every successful property execution and is never reset. When the same test class is executed more than once in the same JVM (e.g. the harness re-runs boxOfFoo), the JUnitQuickcheck runner reloads the nested class state only once, so the accumulated counter carries over from the previous run. The first run leaves iterations at 100; the second run adds another 100, making the assertion of defaultPropertyTrialCount() (100) see 300, producing 'expected:<100> but was:<300>'.

evidence.why: Static field shared across all runs of the test class in the same JVM; it is not reset between executions, so its value persists and accumulates.
The property increments the static counter on every trial (100 trials per run). Repeated runs add 100 each time, so the second/third execution yields 200/300 instead of the expected 100.
Asserts the accumulated static counter equals the per-run trial count (100). Because the counter is never cleared, a second run in the same JVM observes 300 and fails.

Under machine load, waitFor's sleep-poll loop never observes the expected condition before the enclosing @Test(timeout=30000) fires, producing the TestTimedOutException.

evidence.why: The failure stack shows the test blocked here at Thread.sleep inside GenericTestUtils.waitFor; the polled condition (renewer thread timeout/expiry) is not reached within the allotted time, so the JUnit 30s test deadline triggers the timeout.

evidence.snippet: @Override public long renew(...) { ... return System.currentTimeMillis() + 3000; ... return 2*1000 + System.currentTimeMillis(); ... return 86400*1000 + System.currentTimeMillis(); }
evidence.why: The renewal back-off timings (2s/3s/86400s) are wall-clock based; the test's wait for the renewer to time out depends on real elapsed time and background thread scheduling, which is exactly the timing nondeterminism that makes it flaky.

history.hypothesis: The test likely depends on mutable static Configuration/seed state in junit-quickcheck, so running it multiple times back-to-back in the same JVM without resetting state can yield a different sampling outcome than a fresh JVM.

diagnosis.root_cause: The WrapperChars test class keeps its iteration count in a mutable static field (`static int iterations`) that is incremented once per generated trial but never reset between executions. When the same test method is executed more than once in the same JVM, the counter accumulates (100 + 100 + 100 = 300), so the assertion `assertEquals(defaultPropertyTrialCount(), WrapperChars.iterations)` at SamplingButAlsoIncludingAGivenSetTest.java:185 fails on the 2nd/3rd re-execution even though the property itself behaved correctly.

evidence.snippet: @Test public void wrapperChars() throws Exception { assertThat(testResult(WrapperChars.class), isSuccessful()); assertEquals(defaultPropertyTrialCount(), WrapperChars.iterations);
evidence.why: This is the assertion reported at line 185 as failing with `expected:<100> but was:<300>`. It reads the static counter, which carries state over from prior executions in the same JVM.

evidence.snippet: public static class WrapperChars { static int iterations; ... @Property public void shouldHold(@Also({"@", "#"}) @From(AChar.class) Character ch) { values.add(ch); ++iterations; } }
evidence.why: `static int iterations` is shared JVM-wide and is only incremented (never reset). Each re-run of testResult(WrapperChars.class) adds another ~100 to the value, so the second execution yields 200 and the third yields 300, producing expected:<100> but was:<300>.
